name: Cell detachment and QC module v1 (demo scale)
description: DEMO SCALE: drawn 90 x 50 mm, scaled uniformly by 0.324 into 30 x 20 mm (depths unchanged at 0.15 mm); channels clamped up to 0.2 mm, ports 0.8 mm at >= 5 mm pitch. 4 ports, so no port merges needed. Capability lost: serpentine cut from 90 to ~12 mm, culture area ~10x smaller. The original design notes follow, quoted at the original 90 x 50 mm scale (the 100 um feature floor there is now the 200 um floor): A deliberately SMALL 90 x 50 mm module: it detaches adherent cells enzymatically, neutralises on the way out, and gives a counting window. It does NOT wash, filter, concentrate or exchange buffer, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Those four steps were costed against a bench tube and lost: at a 100 um feature floor, deterministic lateral displacement needs 12-45 um gaps, impedance counting needs a 20-50 um aperture, a pillar gap that removes 30-40 um clumps is impossible, and the final viscous resuspension (about 75 cP) collapses the Reynolds number by ~75x so inertial focusing stops working altogether. Doing all six steps on chip gives roughly 0.35 cumulative recovery in about 50 min; the two kept here plus a tube give roughly 0.7 in about 30 min. cult_1 is the adherent chamber and the only heated zone; mix_1 is a serpentine that neutralises by co-flowing quench buffer, because diffusion alone across 100 um would take ~100 s; qc_1 is a plain transparent window, 150 um deep, imaged from outside by a phone or USB microscope. Every feature is >= 100 um, one embossing depth, no photolithography. Geometry is ours; the methods it serves are cited in protocols/cell_prep_v1.json.

chambers.note: Adherent growth area, now about 0.32 cm2 (was 3 cm2), roughly 30k cells at typical density, still about 3x the ~10,000 cells this pipeline consumes. The only heated zone on the board.

Serpentine neutralisation, shortened from 90 mm to ~12 mm to fit the scaled 4.5 x 1.9 mm footprint (0.2 mm lanes, 0.4 mm walls). Residence is about 7x shorter at equal flow, so slow the flow. Mixing has to be advective.

Static counting window, 150 um deep, which is about a haemocytometer's depth. Stopped-flow, imaged from outside. Counting ~400 cells gives a 5% Poisson CV, and a 20% concentration error only moves single-capsule occupancy by about 15%, so this is accurate enough and an in-line counter is not worth building.

ports.note: To a chilled tube. Everything after this is bench: spin, 40 um strainer, resuspend.
